intro: You already know formal words and how to write a formal letter. Now you'll learn to shift: the same message written for a ministry, a client and a friend, and how to choose the right register for each reader and each app. Warm-up: how would you tell your team on WhatsApp that tomorrow's meeting is postponed?
teachingNotes: Recap in one line, don't re-teach: b2-formal-informal-vocab (formal partners like get → receive, help → assist; phrasal verb → Latin-based verb: find out → discover, put off → postpone, look into → investigate; Mr / Ms + surname), b2-formal-writing (no contractions, the passive, Yours sincerely / faithfully, 'Please be informed' and 'Herewith' sound old-fashioned), c1-connotation (same formality, different feeling) and c1-collocations (strong partners for reports). New here: register (tingkat formalitas) as a line with three points (formal, neutral, informal) and the skill of SHIFTING a whole message along it for a given audience and channel. Neutral is the everyday work register; most learners know formal and informal but not the middle.

Features to stress. Formal (reports, letters to officials, academic writing, a first email to a ministry): full forms (I am, we cannot), one-word Latin-based verbs instead of phrasal verbs where one exists (postpone, investigate, tolerate, continue, contact, reduce, resolve), impersonal sentences and the passive (The meeting has been postponed), formal linkers, complete sentences, no emoji or abbreviations. Neutral (most work emails, clients you know, LinkedIn): clear and polite, Could you …?, I'm afraid …, Please let me know, some contractions and common phrasal verbs are fine, Hi + name. Informal (friends, close colleagues, chat apps): contractions, phrasal verbs (put up with, push back, get back to), dropped words (Sounds good. Got it. Running late!), Hey, Cheers (British), emoji only with people you know well. New C1 pairs (informal → formal): put up with → tolerate, carry on → continue, get in touch with → contact, cut down on → reduce, sort out → resolve, turn up → arrive / attend, get back to someone → reply to / respond to; phrases: Sorry, but … → I'm afraid … → I regret to inform you that …; Can you …? → Could you …? → I would be grateful if you could …; asap → as soon as possible → at your earliest convenience; Let me know! → Please let me know → Please inform me.

Choosing a register (objective adapt-register-to): audience (relationship, seniority, culture: Indonesian workplaces are hierarchical, many English-speaking workplaces move to first names quickly, even with senior people), channel (formal letter / official email → formal; work email, LinkedIn message to a stranger → neutral; Slack, Teams, WhatsApp → neutral or informal depending on the person; text to a friend → informal) and purpose (bad news, complaints, apologies, money, anything legal → more careful and formal; quick logistics → shorter). The same person can get different registers on different channels (a report to Bu Ani is formal, an email to her neutral, the team WhatsApp relaxed but respectful). Two safe habits: when unsure, go one step more formal; then follow the other person's lead (if Mr Tan signs 'Best, David', write 'Hi David' next time). Hi is neutral, Hey is informal.

The node's common error and the Indonesian habits: mixing registers in one message is the commonest C1 error: 'Hey Mr Tan, wanna catch up about the contract?' → 'Dear Mr Tan, would you be available to discuss the contract?' (formal) or 'Hi David, could we have a quick chat about the contract?' (neutral, once on first-name terms). Also 'Dear Ms Wong, pls send asap, thx!' and 'I regret to inform you that we can't make it lol'. Too stiff: bahasa baku translated word for word ('We hereby inform you that …' from 'Dengan ini kami beritahukan', 'Herewith we attach …', 'Kindly be informed') → I am writing to inform you that …, Please find attached …. Too casual: WhatsApp style with clients ('Ok sir, noted ya 🙏') → Hi Mr Tan, I've just sent the files. Names: Bapak / Ibu → Mr / Ms + surname (Dear Mr Tan), never Mr + first name (Mr David); on first-name terms just the first name; with Indonesian colleagues Dear Pak Hasan / Bu Ani is the local custom. British Mr / Ms, American Mr. / Ms.

Clefts (from the chain) and register: what-clefts (What we need is a clear deadline) are fine in speech and neutral emails; it-clefts and 'The reason … is that …' sound more written and formal (It is the delivery date that concerns us most); in chat you'd just say 'The delivery date's the problem.' At C1 register is a scale and a matter of style: accept any version that fits the reader (postpone / put off / move in a neutral email; Hi Mr Tan or Dear Mr Tan to a client), and only mark clear cases wrong: chat words in a formal text, stiff legal words in a chat, a mix inside one message, Mr + first name. Praise what fits, then correct ONE thing.

Limits: A0–B2 grammar plus the chain (cleft sentences, collocations). No inversion ('Should you have any questions' only as a phrase to remember, better avoided), no subjunctive, no impersonal passives (It is expected that …) and no nominalisation as a topic. Dropped words in chat are taught only as chunks (Sounds good, Got it, Running late, See you there), not as the ellipsis lesson. Don't teach slang beyond common chat words (mate, no way, gonna / wanna as things to avoid at work). Contexts: Jakarta, Bandung and Surabaya offices, ministries, clients in Singapore, LinkedIn recruiters, team WhatsApp groups, Slack and Teams.

keyPoints.title: Choose the register for the reader and the channel
keyPoints.explanation: Register is a line: formal (reports, letters to officials, academic writing: full forms, one-word verbs, the passive), neutral (most work emails, LinkedIn: clear and polite, some contractions) and informal (friends, chat apps: contractions, phrasal verbs, Sounds good, emoji only with friends). Choose by audience (relationship, seniority, culture), channel (letter, email, Slack, Teams, WhatsApp, LinkedIn, text) and purpose (bad news and money need more care). The same person can get different registers on different channels. Not sure? Go one step more formal, then follow their lead. Don't mix registers in one message.

id.title: Pilih register sesuai pembaca dan media
id.explanation: Register itu sebuah garis: formal (laporan, surat ke instansi, tulisan akademik: bentuk lengkap, kata kerja satu kata, kalimat pasif), netral (kebanyakan email kerja, LinkedIn: jelas dan sopan, boleh sedikit singkatan seperti I'm) dan informal (teman, aplikasi chat: singkatan, phrasal verb, Sounds good, emoji hanya dengan teman). Pilih berdasarkan audiens (seberapa dekat, seberapa senior, budayanya), media (surat, email, Slack, Teams, WhatsApp, LinkedIn, SMS) dan tujuan (kabar buruk dan urusan uang perlu lebih hati-hati). Orang yang sama bisa mendapat register berbeda di media berbeda. Ragu? Naikkan satu tingkat lebih formal, lalu ikuti gaya mereka. Jangan mencampur register dalam satu pesan.

keyPoints.title: Rewrite one message in three registers
keyPoints.explanation: To shift a message, change the greeting, the verbs (postpone → put off → push back), contractions, the person (the passive in formal, we and I in neutral and informal), the length and the sign-off. Formal: I regret to inform you that the meeting has been postponed until further notice. Neutral: I'm afraid we need to postpone the meeting. I'll send a new date soon. Informal: Hey, we'll have to push the meeting back, new date soon! Useful pairs (informal → formal): put up with → tolerate, carry on → continue, get in touch with → contact, cut down on → reduce, sort out → resolve; Sorry, but … → I'm afraid … → I regret to inform you that …; Let me know! → Please let me know → Please inform me.

examples.en: I would be grateful if you could send the signed contract at your earliest convenience.
examples.id: Kami akan sangat berterima kasih jika Bapak/Ibu dapat mengirimkan kontrak yang sudah ditandatangani secepatnya.

examples.en: Could you send me the signed contract when you get a chance?
examples.id: Bisa kirimkan kontrak yang sudah ditandatangani kalau sempat?

id.title: Menulis ulang satu pesan dalam tiga register
id.explanation: Untuk menggeser register sebuah pesan, ubah salamnya, kata kerjanya (postpone → put off → push back), singkatan seperti I'm, siapa pelakunya (pasif di formal, we dan I di netral dan informal), panjangnya, dan salam penutupnya. Formal: I regret to inform you that the meeting has been postponed until further notice. Netral: I'm afraid we need to postpone the meeting. I'll send a new date soon. Informal: Hey, we'll have to push the meeting back, new date soon! Pasangan yang berguna (informal → formal): put up with → tolerate (menoleransi), carry on → continue (melanjutkan), get in touch with → contact (menghubungi), cut down on → reduce (mengurangi), sort out → resolve (menyelesaikan); Sorry, but … → I'm afraid … → I regret to inform you that …; Let me know! → Please let me know → Please inform me.

assessment.prompt: Make this sentence for a formal company announcement more formal. Replace 'put off' with ONE verb in the same form: 'The board has decided to put off the vote on the merger until March.'
assessment.rubric: Correct: postpone (= put off: it still happens, later); defer and delay are also natural. 'postponed' / 'postponing' = 70 (right verb, wrong form after 'decided to'). 'cancel' = 0 (a different meaning: call off, it won't happen). 'push back' = 30 (same meaning but still a phrasal verb, so not more formal).

assessment.prompt: This sentence is going into an official audit report. Replace 'look into' with ONE formal verb in the same form: 'The ministry will look into the complaints about the new toll road.'
assessment.rubric: Correct: investigate (= look into a problem or complaint); examine and review are also fine. 'investigate into' = 60 (right verb, but the formal verb takes no small word). 'investigates' / 'investigated' = 70 (wrong form after will). 'check' = 40 (correct meaning but neutral, not formal). 'see' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Rewrite this line for a formal HR policy document. Replace 'put up with' with ONE verb: 'The company will not put up with bullying of any kind.'
assessment.rubric: Correct: tolerate (= put up with: accept something unpleasant); accept and condone are also natural here. 'tolerates' / 'tolerated' = 70 (wrong form after will not). 'allow' = 70 (close meaning, a little weaker). 'stand' = 30 (informal: can't stand). 'bear with' = 0 (a different meaning: be patient).

assessment.prompt: Your formal draft to a colleague says: 'Please inform me if the client changes the deadline.' Make it neutral for a normal work email: replace 'inform me' with a common three-word phrase.
acceptableAnswers: please let me know if the client changes the deadline
let me know if the client changes the deadline
assessment.rubric: Correct: let me know (Please let me know if …), the normal neutral phrase in work emails. 'tell me' = 70 (right meaning, two words, a bit direct). 'keep me posted' / 'keep me updated' = 80 (natural, slightly informal). 'inform to me' = 0 (the Indonesian trap from 'menginformasikan kepada'). 'notify me' = 20 (still formal).

assessment.prompt: Rina is writing to a new client in Singapore. One word in her email is from a chat, not an email. Write that word. 'Dear Mr Lim, Thank you for your quick reply. I wanna confirm that the samples will arrive in Singapore on Monday. Kind regards, Rina'
assessment.rubric: Correct: wanna (a spoken / chat form of 'want to'; in this email: 'I would like to confirm' or 'I am writing to confirm'). Writing the fix instead of the word ('would like to', 'want to') = 80 (the learner found the problem). 'quick' / 'Dear' / 'Kind regards' = 0 (these fit a client email).

assessment.prompt: Which register fits best: formal, neutral or informal? A letter to the Directorate General of Immigration asking to extend a foreign colleague's work permit.
assessment.rubric: Correct: formal (an official reader you don't know, a legal matter: full forms, one-word verbs, no contractions). 'neutral' = 30 (polite, but too relaxed for a government office). 'informal' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Which register fits best: formal, neutral or informal? An email to Ms Chen, a client you have worked with for two years, confirming the time of next Tuesday's video call.
assessment.rubric: Correct: neutral (a work email to someone you know well about simple logistics: clear and polite, e.g. 'Hi Ms Chen, just confirming our call on Tuesday at 10 a.m.'). 'formal' = 50 (not wrong, but too stiff for a two-year relationship and a quick confirmation). 'informal' = 30 (she is still a client).

blocks.text:
Quick recap: at B2 you swapped everyday words for formal partners (*find out → discover, help → assist*) and wrote formal letters and reports (no contractions, the passive, *Yours sincerely*). In the connotation lesson you chose words by their feeling.

At C1 the new skill is **shifting**. **Register** (tingkat formalitas bahasa) is not two boxes, formal and informal: think of **a line** with three main points.

- **Formal**: reports, letters to officials, academic writing, a first email to a ministry. **Full forms** (*I am, we cannot*); **one-word verbs** from Latin instead of phrasal verbs where one exists (*postpone, investigate, tolerate*); **impersonal** sentences and the **passive** (*The results will be announced on 3 March.*); formal linkers (*However, Consequently*); complete sentences, no emoji.
- **Neutral**: most work emails, clients you know, LinkedIn. **Clear and polite**: *Could you …?, I'm afraid …, Please let me know*. Some contractions (*I'm, we'll*) and common phrasal verbs are fine. *Hi* + name.
- **Informal**: friends, close colleagues, chat apps. Contractions, phrasal verbs (*push back, get back to*), **dropped words** (*Sounds good. Got it. Running late!*: the *That / I* at the start disappears), *Hey*, and emoji, but **only with people you know well**.

id.text:
Pengingat singkat: di B2 kamu mengganti kata sehari-hari dengan pasangan formalnya (*find out → discover, help → assist*) dan menulis surat serta laporan formal (tanpa singkatan, kalimat pasif, *Yours sincerely*). Di pelajaran konotasi kamu memilih kata berdasarkan 'rasa'-nya.

Di C1 keterampilan barunya adalah **menggeser**. **Register** (tingkat formalitas bahasa) bukan dua kotak, formal dan informal: bayangkan **sebuah garis** dengan tiga titik utama.

- **Formal**: laporan, surat ke instansi, tulisan akademik, email pertama ke kementerian. **Bentuk lengkap** (*I am, we cannot*); **kata kerja satu kata** dari bahasa Latin, bukan phrasal verb, kalau ada (*postpone, investigate, tolerate*); kalimat **impersonal** (tidak menonjolkan orangnya) dan **pasif** (*The results will be announced on 3 March.*); kata penghubung formal (*However, Consequently*); kalimat lengkap, tanpa emoji.
- **Netral**: kebanyakan email kerja, klien yang sudah kamu kenal, LinkedIn. **Jelas dan sopan**: *Could you …?, I'm afraid …, Please let me know*. Boleh sedikit singkatan (*I'm, we'll*, disebut contraction) dan phrasal verb yang umum. *Hi* + nama.
- **Informal**: teman, rekan yang akrab, aplikasi chat. Singkatan, phrasal verb (*push back, get back to*), **kata yang dihilangkan** (*Sounds good. Got it. Running late!*: *That / I* di awal kalimat hilang), *Hey*, dan emoji, tapi **hanya dengan orang yang sudah akrab**.

blocks.text:
**Neutral is your everyday work register.** Most workplace English is neither stiff nor chatty. *Hi* is neutral; *Hey* is informal.

**Not sure? Go one step more formal** than you think: it's easy to relax later, but hard to repair a first message that sounded too casual.

**Formal doesn't mean long.** A short, clear sentence with the right verb (*We will investigate the complaint.*) is better than a long, heavy one. And the line is a **scale**: real emails sit between the points, so there is often more than one good choice.

id.text:
**Netral adalah register sehari-hari di kantor.** Kebanyakan bahasa Inggris di tempat kerja tidak kaku dan tidak terlalu santai. *Hi* itu netral; *Hey* itu informal.

**Ragu? Naikkan satu tingkat lebih formal** dari dugaanmu: gampang untuk santai belakangan, tapi susah memperbaiki pesan pertama yang terdengar terlalu santai.

**Formal bukan berarti panjang.** Kalimat pendek dan jelas dengan kata kerja yang tepat (*We will investigate the complaint.*) lebih baik daripada kalimat panjang yang berat. Dan garis ini adalah **skala**: email sungguhan sering ada di antara titik-titiknya, jadi sering ada lebih dari satu pilihan yang baik.

blocks.prompt: Which sentence is NEUTRAL, right for most work emails?
options: Could you send me the updated figures by Thursday?
We hereby request the submission of the updated figures.
blocks.explain: Could you …? is clear and polite: the neutral request. 'hereby' sounds like a legal document (too stiff), and 'Thurs? Thx' is chat (too casual for most emails).

id.prompt: Kalimat mana yang NETRAL, cocok untuk kebanyakan email kerja?
id.explain: Could you …? jelas dan sopan: permintaan yang netral. 'hereby' terdengar seperti dokumen hukum (terlalu kaku), dan 'Thurs? Thx' itu gaya chat (terlalu santai untuk kebanyakan email).

blocks.text:
Before you write, ask three questions.

**1. Audience** (audiens: who is reading?)
- How well do you know them? A director you've never met → formal; a client you've worked with for a year → neutral; a teammate who is also a friend → informal.
- How senior are they, and what's the **culture**? Indonesian workplaces are quite hierarchical (*Pak / Bu* even for seniors you know well). In many English-speaking workplaces, people move to **first names** quickly, even with the boss, but they stay polite.

**2. Channel** (media: how are you sending it?)
- formal letter, official email → **formal**
- work email, a LinkedIn message to someone you don't know → **neutral**
- Slack, Teams, WhatsApp → **neutral or informal**, depending on the person
- a text to a friend → **informal**

**3. Purpose** (tujuan: why are you writing?)
- bad news, a complaint, an apology, money, anything legal → more careful and more formal
- quick logistics (*I'm five minutes late*) → shorter and less formal

**The same person can get different registers on different channels.** Rina writes a formal report to Bu Ani, the Finance Director, a neutral email to her the same day, and a short, polite reply in the team WhatsApp group.

id.text:
Sebelum menulis, ajukan tiga pertanyaan.

**1. Audiens** (audience: siapa yang membaca?)
- Seberapa kenal kamu dengan mereka? Direktur yang belum pernah kamu temui → formal; klien yang sudah setahun bekerja sama → netral; rekan satu tim yang juga teman → informal.
- Seberapa senior mereka, dan bagaimana **budayanya**? Tempat kerja di Indonesia cukup hierarkis (*Pak / Bu* bahkan untuk atasan yang sudah akrab). Di banyak tempat kerja berbahasa Inggris, orang cepat beralih ke **nama depan**, bahkan dengan bos, tapi tetap sopan.

**2. Media** (channel: lewat apa kamu mengirimnya?)
- surat formal, email resmi → **formal**
- email kerja, pesan LinkedIn ke orang yang belum kamu kenal → **netral**
- Slack, Teams, WhatsApp → **netral atau informal**, tergantung orangnya
- SMS ke teman → **informal**

**3. Tujuan** (purpose: kenapa kamu menulis?)
- kabar buruk, keluhan, permintaan maaf, uang, apa pun yang menyangkut hukum → lebih hati-hati dan lebih formal
- urusan teknis singkat (*I'm five minutes late*) → lebih pendek dan kurang formal

**Orang yang sama bisa mendapat register berbeda di media berbeda.** Rina menulis laporan formal untuk Bu Ani, Direktur Keuangan, email netral kepadanya di hari yang sama, dan balasan singkat yang sopan di grup WhatsApp tim.

blocks.text:
**A chat app isn't automatically informal.** A WhatsApp to a client or a director is still work: full words, no slang, and emoji only if they use them first.

**Follow their lead** (ikuti gaya mereka). Start a step more formal, then copy the other person: if Mr Tan signs his reply *Best, David*, you can start your next email *Hi David,*. If a client keeps writing *Dear Ms Putri,*, stay formal too.

id.text:
**Aplikasi chat tidak otomatis informal.** WhatsApp ke klien atau direktur tetap urusan kerja: kata lengkap, tanpa bahasa gaul, dan emoji hanya kalau mereka memakainya duluan.

**Ikuti gaya mereka** (follow their lead). Mulai satu tingkat lebih formal, lalu tiru lawan bicaramu: kalau Mr Tan menutup balasannya dengan *Best, David*, email berikutnya boleh kamu mulai dengan *Hi David,*. Kalau klien terus menulis *Dear Ms Putri,*, tetaplah formal juga.

blocks.prompt: You're sending a Teams message to Pak Hasan, a senior manager you rarely talk to, about a change in tomorrow's schedule. Which opening fits best?
options: Good morning, Pak Hasan. A quick update on tomorrow's schedule:
Dear Sir, I hereby notify you of a change in tomorrow's schedule.
blocks.explain: Teams is a chat app, but Pak Hasan is senior and not a close friend: a polite, neutral opening with his name. 'Hey! Quick one' is for a teammate you know well; 'Dear Sir, I hereby notify' is a stiff letter, not a chat.

id.prompt: Kamu mengirim pesan Teams ke Pak Hasan, manajer senior yang jarang kamu ajak bicara, tentang perubahan jadwal besok. Pembuka mana yang paling cocok?
id.explain: Teams memang aplikasi chat, tapi Pak Hasan senior dan bukan teman akrab: pembuka netral dan sopan dengan namanya. 'Hey! Quick one' untuk rekan tim yang akrab; 'Dear Sir, I hereby notify' itu surat yang kaku, bukan chat.

blocks.text:
To shift a message along the line, change these parts: the **greeting** (*Dear Mr Tan → Hi David → Hey!*), the **verbs** (one-word formal verb ↔ phrasal verb), **contractions**, the **person** (the passive or *we* in formal, *I / we* in neutral, dropped words in informal), the **length** and the **sign-off**.

Example: a meeting is postponed.
- **Formal**: *I regret to inform you that the meeting has been postponed until further notice.*
- **Neutral**: *I'm afraid we need to postpone the meeting. I'll send a new date soon.*
- **Informal**: *Hey, we'll have to push the meeting back, new date soon!*

At B2 you met *find out → discover, look into → investigate, put off → postpone*. More pairs (informal → formal):
- **put up with → tolerate** (menoleransi, membiarkan)
- **carry on → continue** (melanjutkan)
- **get in touch with → contact** (menghubungi)
- **cut down on → reduce** (mengurangi)
- **sort out → resolve** (menyelesaikan masalah)
- **turn up → arrive / attend** (datang, hadir)
- **get back to someone → reply to / respond to** (membalas, mengabari)

And whole phrases (informal → neutral → formal):
- *Sorry, but …* → *I'm afraid …* → *I regret to inform you that …*
- *Can you …?* → *Could you …?* → *I would be grateful if you could …*
- *asap* → *as soon as possible* → *at your earliest convenience*
- *Let me know!* → *Please let me know* → *Please inform me*

id.text:
Untuk menggeser sebuah pesan di sepanjang garis, ubah bagian-bagian ini: **salam** (*Dear Mr Tan → Hi David → Hey!*), **kata kerja** (kata kerja formal satu kata ↔ phrasal verb), **singkatan** (contraction), **pelaku** (pasif atau *we* di formal, *I / we* di netral, kata dihilangkan di informal), **panjang** pesan, dan **salam penutup**.

Contoh: rapat ditunda.
- **Formal**: *I regret to inform you that the meeting has been postponed until further notice.*
- **Netral**: *I'm afraid we need to postpone the meeting. I'll send a new date soon.*
- **Informal**: *Hey, we'll have to push the meeting back, new date soon!*

Di B2 kamu sudah bertemu *find out → discover, look into → investigate, put off → postpone*. Pasangan lain (informal → formal):
- **put up with → tolerate** (menoleransi, membiarkan)
- **carry on → continue** (melanjutkan)
- **get in touch with → contact** (menghubungi)
- **cut down on → reduce** (mengurangi)
- **sort out → resolve** (menyelesaikan masalah)
- **turn up → arrive / attend** (datang, hadir)
- **get back to someone → reply to / respond to** (membalas, mengabari)

Dan frasa utuh (informal → netral → formal):
- *Sorry, but …* → *I'm afraid …* → *I regret to inform you that …*
- *Can you …?* → *Could you …?* → *I would be grateful if you could …*
- *asap* → *as soon as possible* → *at your earliest convenience*
- *Let me know!* → *Please let me know* → *Please inform me*

rows.id: Kami akan sangat berterima kasih jika Bapak/Ibu dapat mengirimkan kontrak yang sudah ditandatangani secepatnya.

blocks.text:
**Clefts and register.** A what-cleft (*What we need is a clear deadline.*) is natural in meetings and in neutral emails. An it-cleft (*It is the delivery date that concerns us most.*) and *The reason … is that …* sound more written and formal. In a chat you'd just say *The delivery date's the problem.*

**Check every part.** When you shift a message, change all of it: a formal verb with a chat greeting (*Hey Mr Lim, we regret …*) is a mix.

id.text:
**Kalimat cleft dan register.** What-cleft (*What we need is a clear deadline.*) terdengar alami dalam rapat dan email netral. It-cleft (*It is the delivery date that concerns us most.*) dan *The reason … is that …* terdengar lebih tertulis dan formal. Di chat kamu cukup bilang *The delivery date's the problem.*

**Periksa setiap bagian.** Saat menggeser register sebuah pesan, ubah semuanya: kata kerja formal dengan salam gaya chat (*Hey Mr Lim, we regret …*) itu campuran.

blocks.prompt: Which is the most FORMAL version of 'We'll carry on checking the river levels'?
options: We'll keep checking the river levels.
We will continue to monitor the river levels.
We will carry on to monitor the river levels.
blocks.explain: continue (the formal partner of carry on), full form 'We will', and the precise verb monitor. 'We'll keep checking' is neutral. 'carry on to monitor' is wrong: carry on takes -ing (carry on checking), and it is still a phrasal verb.

id.prompt: Mana versi yang paling FORMAL dari 'We'll carry on checking the river levels'?
id.explain: continue (pasangan formal carry on), bentuk lengkap 'We will', dan kata kerja yang tepat: monitor. 'We'll keep checking' itu netral. 'carry on to monitor' salah: carry on diikuti -ing (carry on checking), dan tetap phrasal verb.

id.title: Jangan campur register: kebiasaan dari bahasa Indonesia

blocks.text:
The commonest C1 error isn't a grammar mistake. It's **mixing registers** in one message:
- *Hey Mr Tan, wanna catch up about the contract?* ✗ *Hey, wanna* and *catch up* are chat; *Mr Tan* is formal.
  → formal: *Dear Mr Tan, would you be available to discuss the contract?*
  → neutral (once you're on first-name terms): *Hi David, could we have a quick chat about the contract?*
- *Dear Ms Wong, pls send asap, thx!* ✗ → *Dear Ms Wong, could you please send it as soon as possible? Thank you.*
- *I regret to inform you that we can't make it lol* ✗

Pick **one point on the line** and stay there.

**Indonesian habits that cause mixes:**
1) **Too stiff**: bahasa baku translated word for word. *Dengan ini kami beritahukan bahwa …* → `We hereby inform you that …` (sounds like a legal contract). *Bersama ini kami lampirkan* → `Herewith we attach`. Modern formal English is **plainer** than formal Indonesian: *I am writing to inform you that …*, *Please find attached …*, *Thank you for your time.*
2) **Too casual**: WhatsApp style with clients. `Ok sir, noted ya 🙏 sdh sy kirim` → *Hi Mr Tan, I've just sent the files. Please let me know if anything is missing.* No *ya*, no *sir* in writing, no abbreviations, and emoji only if the client uses them first.
3) **Names**: *Bapak / Ibu* → **Mr / Ms + surname** (*Dear Mr Tan*), never Mr + first name (`Mr David`). On first-name terms: just the name (*Hi David*). With Indonesian colleagues, *Dear Pak Hasan / Bu Ani* is the local custom. British English writes *Mr / Ms*, American English *Mr. / Ms.*

id.text:
Kesalahan paling umum di C1 bukan kesalahan tata bahasa. Kesalahannya adalah **mencampur register** dalam satu pesan:
- *Hey Mr Tan, wanna catch up about the contract?* ✗ *Hey, wanna* dan *catch up* itu gaya chat; *Mr Tan* itu formal.
  → formal: *Dear Mr Tan, would you be available to discuss the contract?*
  → netral (kalau sudah saling panggil nama depan): *Hi David, could we have a quick chat about the contract?*
- *Dear Ms Wong, pls send asap, thx!* ✗ → *Dear Ms Wong, could you please send it as soon as possible? Thank you.*
- *I regret to inform you that we can't make it lol* ✗

Pilih **satu titik di garis** dan tetaplah di situ.

**Kebiasaan dari bahasa Indonesia yang membuat campuran:**
1) **Terlalu kaku**: bahasa baku diterjemahkan kata per kata. *Dengan ini kami beritahukan bahwa …* → `We hereby inform you that …` (terdengar seperti kontrak hukum). *Bersama ini kami lampirkan* → `Herewith we attach`. Bahasa Inggris formal modern **lebih sederhana** daripada bahasa Indonesia formal: *I am writing to inform you that …*, *Please find attached …*, *Thank you for your time.*
2) **Terlalu santai**: gaya WhatsApp ke klien. `Ok sir, noted ya 🙏 sdh sy kirim` → *Hi Mr Tan, I've just sent the files. Please let me know if anything is missing.* Tanpa *ya*, tanpa *sir* dalam tulisan, tanpa singkatan, dan emoji hanya kalau klien memakainya duluan.
3) **Nama**: *Bapak / Ibu* → **Mr / Ms + nama keluarga** (*Dear Mr Tan*), jangan pernah Mr + nama depan (`Mr David`). Kalau sudah saling panggil nama depan: cukup namanya (*Hi David*). Dengan rekan orang Indonesia, *Dear Pak Hasan / Bu Ani* adalah kebiasaan setempat. Bahasa Inggris British menulis *Mr / Ms*, Amerika *Mr. / Ms.*

rows.en: I am writing to inform you that our office will move to Bandung in July.
rows.id: Dengan ini kami beritahukan bahwa kantor kami akan pindah ke Bandung pada bulan Juli.

rows.en: Please find attached the minutes of yesterday's meeting.
rows.id: Bersama ini kami lampirkan notulen rapat kemarin.

rows.en: Hi Mr Tan, I've just sent the files. Please let me know if anything is missing.
rows.id: Pak Tan, filenya sudah saya kirim ya. Kabari saya kalau ada yang kurang.
Atas perhatiannya kami ucapkan terima kasih.

blocks.text: **Quick test before you press Send:** read only the greeting, the verbs and the sign-off. Do they all belong to the same point on the line? *Dear … / postpone / Kind regards* ✓. *Hey … / postpone / Cheers* is fine for a friend. *Dear … / wanna / thx* ✗.

id.text: **Tes cepat sebelum menekan Kirim:** baca hanya salam pembuka, kata kerja, dan salam penutupnya. Apakah semuanya berada di titik yang sama di garis? *Dear … / postpone / Kind regards* ✓. *Hey … / postpone / Cheers* tidak masalah untuk teman. *Dear … / wanna / thx* ✗.

blocks.prompt: You're emailing Sarah Lim, a client you've worked with for a year. She signs her emails 'Best, Sarah'. Which greeting fits?
blocks.explain: She signs with her first name, so follow her lead: Hi + first name. 'Ms Sarah' and 'Madam Sarah' put a title before a first name, which English doesn't do (Ms goes with the surname: Ms Lim).

id.prompt: Kamu menulis email ke Sarah Lim, klien yang sudah setahun bekerja sama denganmu. Ia menutup emailnya dengan 'Best, Sarah'. Salam pembuka mana yang cocok?
id.explain: Ia memakai nama depannya, jadi ikuti gayanya: Hi + nama depan. 'Ms Sarah' dan 'Madam Sarah' memasang gelar di depan nama depan, dan bahasa Inggris tidak begitu (Ms dipasangkan dengan nama keluarga: Ms Lim).

suggestedQuestions: Is 'Hi Mr Tan' OK in an email to a client?
Can I use contractions like I'm and we'll in a work email?
When can I switch from 'Dear Mr Tan' to 'Hi David'?
Is it OK to use emoji with colleagues?

resources.title: How to Use Formal and Informal English - English Speaking and Writing Fluency
resources.note: A 22-minute lesson built on the same three levels as this lesson (formal, neutral, informal): when to use each, sentence structure, vocabulary, how direct to be, and formal and informal writing. Clear British English; good for listening practice too.

id.note: Pelajaran 22 menit yang memakai tiga tingkat yang sama dengan pelajaran ini (formal, netral, informal): kapan memakai masing-masing, struktur kalimat, kosakata, seberapa langsung kita berbicara, dan tulisan formal serta informal. Bahasa Inggris British yang jelas; bagus juga untuk latihan menyimak.

resources.title: Formal & informal English: Live English Class
resources.note: A 30-minute live class with Sian: four differences between formal and informal English (word pairs, abbreviations, short vs complex sentences, active vs passive) and making an informal email more formal. A free worksheet is linked in the video description.

id.note: Kelas live 30 menit bersama Sian: empat perbedaan bahasa Inggris formal dan informal (pasangan kata, singkatan, kalimat pendek vs kompleks, aktif vs pasif) dan cara membuat email informal menjadi lebih formal. Lembar latihan gratis ada di deskripsi video.

resources.title: English Rewind - 6 Minute English: Formality at work
resources.note: A 6-minute discussion about how formal workplaces are, being on first-name terms with colleagues, and how this has changed. It's about workplace culture rather than writing, so it helps with the 'audience' question.

id.note: Diskusi 6 menit tentang seberapa formal suasana tempat kerja, kebiasaan saling panggil nama depan dengan rekan kerja, dan bagaimana hal itu berubah. Isinya tentang budaya kerja, bukan menulis, jadi membantu menjawab pertanyaan 'siapa audiensnya'.

id.intro: Kamu sudah tahu kata-kata formal dan cara menulis surat formal. Sekarang kamu belajar menggeser register: pesan yang sama ditulis untuk kementerian, klien, dan teman, serta cara memilih register yang tepat untuk setiap pembaca dan setiap aplikasi. Pemanasan: bagaimana kamu memberi tahu timmu lewat WhatsApp bahwa rapat besok ditunda?
suggestedQuestions: Apakah 'Hi Mr Tan' boleh dipakai di email ke klien?
Boleh pakai singkatan seperti I'm dan we'll di email kerja?
Kapan saya boleh beralih dari 'Dear Mr Tan' ke 'Hi David'?
Boleh pakai emoji dengan rekan kerja?

assessment.rgs-1: Buat kalimat untuk pengumuman resmi perusahaan ini lebih formal. Ganti 'put off' dengan SATU kata kerja dalam bentuk yang sama (tulis dalam bahasa Inggris): 'The board has decided to put off the vote on the merger until March.'
assessment.rgs-2: Kalimat ini akan masuk ke laporan audit resmi. Ganti 'look into' dengan SATU kata kerja formal dalam bentuk yang sama (tulis dalam bahasa Inggris): 'The ministry will look into the complaints about the new toll road.'
assessment.rgs-3: Tulis ulang kalimat ini untuk dokumen kebijakan HR yang formal. Ganti 'put up with' dengan SATU kata kerja (tulis dalam bahasa Inggris): 'The company will not put up with bullying of any kind.'
assessment.rgs-4: Draf formalmu untuk seorang rekan berbunyi: 'Please inform me if the client changes the deadline.' Buat jadi netral untuk email kerja biasa: ganti 'inform me' dengan frasa umum tiga kata dalam bahasa Inggris.
assessment.rgs-5: Rina menulis email ke klien baru di Singapura. Ada satu kata di emailnya yang berasal dari gaya chat, bukan email. Tulis kata itu. 'Dear Mr Lim, Thank you for your quick reply. I wanna confirm that the samples will arrive in Singapore on Monday. Kind regards, Rina'
assessment.rgs-6: Register mana yang paling cocok: formal, neutral atau informal? Surat kepada Direktorat Jenderal Imigrasi untuk meminta perpanjangan izin kerja seorang rekan warga negara asing.
assessment.rgs-7: Register mana yang paling cocok: formal, neutral atau informal? Email kepada Ms Chen, klien yang sudah dua tahun bekerja sama denganmu, untuk memastikan jam video call Selasa depan.
